clue.text: Break into chest

definitions.meaning: to break something is to smash or ruin it, as in a broken toy
the bosom or upper front of the body, as in a sculpted head and shoulders

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: smash something and a sculpture or measurement of the upper torso.

clue.text: Count is not noble, I held

indicators.note: one piece is held, gripped inside, by the other

parts.note: base means low-born or ignoble, the opposite of noble

explanation.surface: An aristocrat's claim is denied: the Count is no nobleman, says a speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a title, but it is Count Basie, the American jazz bandleader. The printed grid shows a T at the unchecked fourth square; the wordplay gives I.
explanation.definitionFit: Count was the nickname of jazz pianist and bandleader William Basie, the clue's only definition.

clue.text: Restaurant worker needs miles more training

indicators.note: training licks something into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A waiter has to run extra miles to keep fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine waiter in a restaurant, the staff member who advises on and serves the wine.

clue.text: Sober actor's shocking language

indicators.note: something shocking is outrageous, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A teetotal actor uses outrageously foul language.
explanation.definitionFit: The South Slavic language of the former Yugoslavia, now usually named as separate tongues.

clue.text: Communication of a shared vision

parts.note: reads like a manifesto of common goals, but describes two people looking straight at each other

explanation.definitionFit: Meeting someone's gaze is a wordless form of communication in which two people share a look.

clue.text: One born, about to howl?

parts.note: a newborn is the one likely to start bawling any moment

explanation.definitionFit: An infant, one just born, famously cries loudly as soon as it arrives.

clue.text: To conserve energy, about to hire vehicle

indicators.note: to conserve is to keep safe within, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about
to let is to rent out or hire
brio means vigour or energy

explanation.surface: To save fuel, someone is about to rent a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabriolet is a car with a folding roof, originally a light horse-drawn carriage.

clue.text: Wise young high-flier has left in nothing inept

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, means nothing

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: wet in British slang means feeble or ineffectual

explanation.surface: A clever youngster soars, leaving behind someone useless.
explanation.definitionFit: A young owl, owls being proverbially wise birds that fly high.

clue.text: Try out striker in international

parts.note: to test something is to try it out
a match is struck to light it, so it is a striker

explanation.surface: A forward gets a trial in a national side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' suggests a footballer, but it is the thing struck to make a flame. A TEST MATCH is an international cricket game.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket and rugby an international between national teams is called a test match.

clue.text: Keep William in Scotland

parts.note: a keep is a stronghold, and adding William names the Highland town ... William

explanation.definitionFit: A keep is a castle's main tower, a stronghold, and Fort William is a town in Scotland.

clue.text: Poet's reminiscences of being treated like country-house footman?

definitions.meaning: the title of John Betjeman's verse autobiography of 1960

definitions.text: of being treated like country-house footman?
definitions.meaning: servants in a big house were called by bells rung from the rooms upstairs

explanation.definitionFit: Betjeman's autobiography in verse bears this title, and it also describes servants answering bell calls.

clue.text: Small matter of man's campaign slogan

parts.note: elect is the command on an election poster
Ron is a man's name, so the slogan belongs to him

explanation.surface: A minor point about one candidate's slogan.
explanation.walkthrough: The slogan is 'Elect Ron', the man's call to voters.
explanation.definitionFit: An electron is a tiny particle of matter, smaller than any atom.

clue.text: Injured party's great energy enthralling one court

indicators.note: enthralling holds captive, so one piece is gripped inside the other

parts.note: vim means vigour or great energy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A wronged person's huge energy captivates the bench.
explanation.definitionFit: A victim is the person harmed, the party that suffered the injury.

clue.text: By the way, there may be a snap as you break it

definitions.text: By the way, there may be a snap as you break it

parts.words: By the way, there may be a snap as you break it
parts.note: by the roadside, a speed camera takes a photo when a driver goes too fast

explanation.definitionFit: Breaking the road's legal maximum speed can be caught by a camera taking a snapshot.

clue.text: Start to cross leg, but have to get up

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a leg is a limb

explanation.surface: Crossing your legs first and then having to stand up.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb is to go upward, to ascend or get up a slope.

clue.text: High-spirited friend joining a band

parts.note: cock is old British slang for a mate, as in 'wotcher cock'
a hoop is a circular band

explanation.surface: A cheerful pal signs up with a group of musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Being exultant, crowing with delight, is the meaning of this old idiom.

clue.text: Generous, being flush with bonus for joining up?

definitions.text: being flush with bonus for joining up?
definitions.meaning: a recruit paid a bounty for enlisting is full of bounty

explanation.definitionFit: Bountiful means liberal and open-handed, and punningly full of bounty money.

clue.text: Really excellent work flourished in difficult situation

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a tight spot, a difficult situation
OP, short for opus, means a work
fl. abbreviates floruit, Latin for flourished, used for dates of people

explanation.surface: Some excellent work thrived in a tough spot.
explanation.walkthrough: TIGHT is used as in 'in a tight spot'; FL is the reference-book abbreviation for floruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The top flight is the highest division, so anything so described is first-rate.

clue.text: One of a titled brotherhood, claimant to throne in the house of Savoy?

definitions.text: One of a titled brotherhood, claimant to throne in the house of Savoy?

parts.words: One of a titled brotherhood, claimant to throne in the house of Savoy?
parts.note: a Gilbert and Sullivan Savoy opera is titled after two Venetian boatman brothers, one of whom may be heir to a throne

explanation.definitionFit: In the Savoy opera by Gilbert and Sullivan, two Venetian boatmen are possible heirs to a kingdom.

clue.text: Gem of a vehicle used by bachelor relative

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in BA
an uncle is a relative

explanation.surface: A jewel of a car being driven by an unmarried uncle.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbuncle is a red gemstone, typically a garnet cut with a rounded top.

clue.text: Head away from smell of rotting fish

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which goes away

parts.note: a stench is a foul smell of decay

explanation.surface: Walk away from the stink of decaying fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A tench is a freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Does not deny it is past the year 1000

indicators.note: past means coming after, so this piece follows

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks a year
M is the Roman numeral for 1000
it's is short for it is

explanation.surface: Someone concedes that the first millennium has gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit something is to accept it as true rather than deny it.

clue.text: Saw job in garage — see to finishing it?

indicators.note: this piece comes at the finish, after the other

parts.note: the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test done in a garage
taken as written

explanation.surface: A garage mechanic is told to finish the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a tool or past tense but is a saying. The MOT is Britain's yearly vehicle safety test.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, much the same as a motto.

clue.text: Faint, or complete dark

definitions.meaning: a sudden loss of consciousness, a swoon
total darkness, as when lights are put out in wartime

explanation.definitionFit: A loss of consciousness and a total extinguishing of lights both go by this name.

clue.text: From which sack may be poured?

definitions.text: From which sack may be poured?

indicators.note: pouring letters out lets them fall into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Asking what container holds the old Spanish sherry known as sack.
explanation.walkthrough: Sack is an old word for dry white wine such as sherry, which was stored in barrels.
explanation.definitionFit: A cask is a barrel, from which wine such as sack is poured.

clue.text: Volunteers to arrest some Russian girl

indicators.note: arresting holds a piece fast within the other

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
any can mean some, as in 'have you any'

explanation.surface: Reservists detain a young Russian woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanya is a Russian girl's name, the pet form of Tatiana.

clue.text: Chinese gang not up to good?

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether some Chinese criminals are not up to any good.
explanation.definitionFit: A tong is a Chinese secret society, often linked with organised crime.

clue.text: Not able to work from instruction

definitions.meaning: read literally, coming out of a commission, an order or brief

explanation.definitionFit: Something broken is said to be out of service, and a commission is also an instruction or order.

clue.text: Debauched snap of girl confiscated by head

indicators.note: what is confiscated is taken and held by the other piece

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head

indicators.note: a snap breaks something, so these letters are broken up

explanation.surface: Someone dissolute has their photo of a girl seized by the headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snap' looks like a photograph, but here it is the anagram signal, breaking up the letters of OF GIRL.
explanation.definitionFit: A profligate is recklessly extravagant and dissolute, a debauched spendthrift.

clue.text: Boat's quiet path cut short

parts.note: P stands for piano, quiet in music

indicators.note: cutting a word short drops its last letter

parts.note: a road is a path or way

explanation.surface: A boat travels along a calm, abbreviated channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A proa is a Malay sailing boat with an outrigger.
